response.justification: While the candidate demonstrates strong full-stack engineering capabilities and excellent communication skills, they lack the core technical requirements for this role. The position requires active hands-on C++ development with 8-12 years of experience, but the candidate's C++ work ended over 10 years ago (6 months at National Instruments in 2014-2015). Their extensive recent experience is in web technologies (TypeScript, Node.js, React). Critically, there is no evidence of industrial automation domain expertise, secure development practices (SDL, IEC 62443), industrial cybersecurity knowledge, or experience with required protocols (Modbus, IEC 61850, etc.). The candidate would require substantial ramp-up in the core technical domain.
strengths: Proven ability to master diverse programming languages and technologies across multiple domains (web, embedded, mobile, backend systems)
Strong communication and mentoring capabilities demonstrated through workshops, talks, and open-source contributions; experience with software craftsmanship and TDD
Experience building high-performance, low-latency systems with async I/O and real-time databases at Dunnhumby, showing systems-level thinking
concerns: C++ expertise is severely outdated: only 6 months of hands-on C++ experience ending in 2015; most recent 10+ years focused on TypeScript, Node.js, and web technologies
Complete absence of industrial automation, embedded systems, or IoT domain knowledge; no experience with required industrial protocols (Modbus TCP/IP, IEC 61850, IEC 104, OPC UA, DNP 3.0)
No demonstrated security expertise: no mention of SDL practices, IEC 62443 compliance, or secure coding methodologies critical for this industrial role

key_factors.factor: Demonstrated technical learning ability across domains
